omissions.description: The source gives specific category-page content and interaction guidance beyond classifying the page's purpose.
omissions.quote:
- Clear subcategories that reduce mental load

- Strong visual hierarchy to support scanning

- Filters that narrow options without overwhelming

- The ability to click through to individual product pages for detail

omissions.description: The source advises monitoring category-page exit rate against the site average to detect design failures.
omissions.quote: Category pages should have an exit rate similar to or near the site average. A high exit rate indicates visitors are leaving the site rather than navigating to product pages—a sign that something in the design is failing.

omissions.description: The source provides mobile category-page design requirements, including thumb-zone placement, tap-target size, rapid filter access, initial-view density, swipe interactions, and image-loading practices.
omissions.quote:
| Thumb-zone ergonomics | Key actions in lower half of screen | Sticky filter bar at bottom |

| Tap targets | Minimum 44px hit area | Generous whitespace |

| Filter access | 75% of mobile users abandon if they cannot refine quickly | Sticky bottom sheet or floating "Filter" pill |

| Above-fold density | First two rows get most taps | Limit hero banners to 30–40% of initial view |

| Swipe interaction | Swiping cards feels more natural than scrolling | Swipeable carousels for subcategories/variants |

| Image loading | Large images slow TTI | Responsive WebP and lazy-load below fold |

omissions.description: The source advises keeping promotional messaging consistent between category pages and PDPs.
omissions.quote: when promo messaging resonates on category pages and is reinforced on PDPs, it increases the likelihood of add-to-cart and can influence the entire purchase conversion rate.

omissions.description: The source specifically recommends keeping the primary PDP Add to Cart CTA visible without scrolling and keeping shipping and return information accessible without navigation away from the page.
omissions.quote: Keeping the primary CTA visible without scrolling reduces friction. Key info (shipping, returns) should be easy to find without navigating away.

omissions.description: The source offers PDP trust and social-proof guidance, including authentic balanced reviews and influencer UGC.
omissions.quote: Customer reviews—authentic, balanced feedback—build credibility. A mix of 4- and 5-star reviews feels more real than a wall of perfect scores. Influencer UGC adds aspirational context.

omissions.description: The source includes a documented GoodwillFinds PDP A/B-test result that is not represented.
omissions.quote: **GoodwillFinds**: A/B testing the product page resulted in a **5.16% increase in clicks on the "Add-to-Bag" button** after just 8 days. The variation emerged as the clear winner.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins at numbered items 2–5, so preceding causal-measurement context is absent.
The excerpt ends immediately after the GoodwillFinds result, so any subsequent PDP guidance or case-study qualifications are unavailable.

Many numerical benchmarks and experimental results are asserted without citations, sample sizes, assignment methods, statistical significance, denominators, or generalizability evidence in this excerpt.
The source gives broad design recommendations but often does not specify implementation criteria, tradeoffs, or validation methods for a particular retailer or visitor segment.
